nodes.summary: For an instance $(n_1, E_1, n_2, E_2, K)$ of MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH, the first graph is the graph of the edge list $E_1$ on $n_1$ vertices: the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n_1 - 1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $E_1$.
nodes.title: First graph of an instance

nodes.summary: For an instance $(n_1, E_1, n_2, E_2, K)$ of MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH, the second graph is the graph of the edge list $E_2$ on $n_2$ vertices: the simple graph on $\{0, \dots, n_2 - 1\}$ in which distinct vertices $i$ and $j$ are adjacent when $(i, j)$ or $(j, i)$ belongs to $E_2$.
nodes.title: Second graph of an instance

nodes.summary: The decision problem MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH accepts a bitstring $x$ exactly when the canonical bitstring decoding of $x$ yields an instance of MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH that is well formed and feasible. Bitstrings that do not decode to an instance are rejected.
nodes.title: MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH as a decision problem

nodes.summary: An instance $(n_1, E_1, n_2, E_2, K)$ of MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH is feasible when, writing $G_1$ and $G_2$ for its first and second graphs, there are a set $A$ of vertices of $G_1$ and a set $B$ of vertices of $G_2$ with $|A| \ge K$ and $|B| = |A|$, and a bijection $f : A \to B$ such that for all $a, b \in A$, the vertices $a$ and $b$ are adjacent in $G_1$ if and only if $f(a)$ and $f(b)$ are adjacent in…
nodes.title: Feasible instances of MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH

nodes.summary: An instance of MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH is a tuple $(n_1, E_1, n_2, E_2, K)$ in which $n_1$, $n_2$ and $K$ are natural numbers and $E_1$, $E_2$ are finite lists of pairs of natural numbers: $n_1$ is the vertex count of the first graph, $E_1$ its edge list, $n_2$ the vertex count of the second graph, $E_2$ its edge list, and $K$ the bound.
nodes.title: Instances of MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH

nodes.summary: The decision problem MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH belongs to NP, and every decision problem in NP reduces to it by a polynomial-time many-one reduction.
nodes.title: MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH is NP-complete

nodes.summary: An instance $(n_1, E_1, n_2, E_2, K)$ of MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH is well formed when, for each $k \in \{1, 2\}$, the list $E_k$ has no repeated entries and every pair $(u, v)$ in $E_k$ has $u < n_k$, $v < n_k$, $u \ne v$ and $(v, u) \notin E_k$.
nodes.title: Well-formed instances of MAXIMUM COMMON INDUCED SUBGRAPH
